summary: Sthaneshwar Timalsina works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1985–1995) and Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg (~2001–2005). He held posts at Nepal Sanskrit University, San Diego State University (~2005–2022), and Stony Brook University (~2022).

Specializing in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies, Wikander studied at Uppsala, Copenhagen, Paris, and Berlin, earning his doctorate under Henrik Samuel Nyberg. He taught at Lund (1941–1953) and held a chair at Uppsala (1953–1974).
Stuart H. Blackburn is an Indologist who studied at Wesleyan University (~1963–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1974–1980). He held a post at SOAS University of London (~1990–2011).

Stuart Piggott was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Churcher's College and the University College London Institute of Archaeology (~1934–1936), later holding a post at the University of Edinburgh (~1946–1977).

Working in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, Sarbacker earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 2001 under David M. Knipe. He held an attested post at Oregon State University in 2018.

Su Bai worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He completed graduate studies at Peking University (1940–1944) under scholars including Rong Geng and Yongtong Tang, and later served as a professor there from 1948 to 2004.

Diskul studied at Chulalongkorn, École du Louvre under Philippe Stern, and UCL. A specialist in history and archaeology, he served as curator at Bangkok's National Museum (~1953–1964) and professor, dean, and rector (1976–1986) at Silpakorn University.

Subhash Kak, active in Indology and other fields, studied at NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi under P. V. Indiresan. He held professorships at Louisiana State University (1979) and Oklahoma State University (2007).

Mitra studied at Utkal University, JNU, and the University of Rochester (~1973–1978). He held academic posts at the University of Hull (~1980–1993), Heidelberg University (~1994–2014), and the National University of Singapore (2015–2018).

Sucheng Chan, working in history and archaeology, studied at Swarthmore College, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and UC Berkeley. She held a post as emerita professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1988–2005).
Sudan Shakya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who held an attested post as a professor at Shuchiin University between 2013 and 2017, and in 2026.

Specializing in religious studies and Indology, Kakar studied at Gujarat University, the University of Mannheim, the University of Vienna, and Sigmund-Freud-Institut. He held posts at Harvard (~1967–1971), IIM Ahmedabad (~1971–1977), and IIT Delhi (1976–1977).

Sudhākara Dvivedī, an Indologist and historian, studied under Devakṛṣṇa. He was a librarian and later professor of mathematics and astrology at Sanskrit College and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, where he headed the mathematics faculty from 1898 to 1905.

Sue Hamilton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She earned her D.Phil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson and Richard Gombrich, and held a post at King's College London (attested 2001–2003).
Suehiro Tanemura studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1957). He later held academic posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1973–1981) and Kokugakuin University (~1986–1998).
Sujeet Kumar works in the fields of computational studies and Indology. He has held academic posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur and B.P. Mandal College of Engineering.

Suk Fun Ng is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014). She studied under teachers including K. L. Dhammajoti, Jing Yin, and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa.

Sukhlal Sanghvi was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Shri Yashovijaya Jain Sanskrit Pathshala and under Balakrishna Mishra. He held posts at Gujarat Vidyapith (1922) and was Chair of Jain Philosophy at Banaras Hindu University (1934–1944).

Sukra Sagar Shrestha was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts as an epigraphist at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1986) and the Department of Archaeology (attested 1987).

Sukumar Sen was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Calcutta under Suniti Kumar Chatterji and Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala. He served at the University of Calcutta as lecturer (1930) and Khaira Professor (1954), and as Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India.
